analysis: Examined four changed items. (1) docs/reference/configuration.md lines 316-317 add two env-var rows, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY. Both are documented as default-on tuning toggles, with off restoring older scheduling. The doc says neither is forwarded to LaunchAgents. They do not touch attestation, authorization, key custody or the coordinator/provider wire contract. I saw no change to the TB-007 posture. The rest of that file's head text is unchanged context. (2) libs/mlx-swift-lm is a submodule pointer bump (0351444e to c66869ea). The submodule diff is not supplied, so the MTP chained-decode and carry changes it presumably contains, along with any other MLX/inference engine changes, are unreviewed. Those affect TB-007 and possibly T-041 prefix-cache correctness, T-028 residual KV data and T-010 cancellation. I cannot conclude they are safe; this is a coverage limit that needs deeper review of the submodule diff. (3) provider-swift/Sources/ProviderBenchmark/RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmark.swift is a new benchmark-only enum, public in the ProviderBenchmark module. It reads a local model directory and hashes weights via WeightHasher. It forces DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=0 in a copied environment, builds sessions through the @_spi(Benchmarking) makeBenchmarkSession with requirePersistentKey=false, and emits JSON containing generated token IDs of public prompts. It handles no consumer data, coordinator keys or attestation, and it opens no network path. Caller-supplied batch sizes are bounded to 1-64 and maxTokens to 131072, and there is an unsupported-MiMo guard. Shutdown and release of the benchmark container happen on both success and error paths. No new attack surface was identified, though how the CLI wires it up is not shown. Remaining question: the actual changes inside the submodule bump, and whether any CLI command exposes the benchmark on a serving path.
